the double-folding potential is more reliable and accurate than the other two models.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the total reaction cross sections for light weakly-bound systems, such as 6He, 8Li, 9Be, 11Be and 11B, are larger than the ones for stable targets, such as 27Al, 51V and 58Ni, and that the reduction methods for total reaction cross sections are not applicable to weakly-bound nuclei.
the total reaction cross sections for light weakly-bound systems are not significantly different from those of stable nuclei.

the total reaction cross sections for the light weakly bound nuclei can be well described by a simple reduction method, i.e., the total reaction cross section of the weakly bound system is equal to the sum of total reaction cross section for the corresponding core nucleus plus the reaction cross section for a single neutron.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the total reaction cross section for 8Li is not a monotonically decreasing function of the binding energy.

the total reaction cross sections for weakly bound systems can be well described by a simple formula which is a function of the binding energy of the projectile and the reduced mass of the system, with no need of the additional reduction factor.
the double folding potential is a better choice than the Woods-Saxon for the analysis of light weakly bound system elastic scattering data.
